photos.question: A client takes furosemide every day for heart failure. Which lab value is most important for the nurse to monitor?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #322!

💧 It pulls off fluid fast, but what else does it pull out?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Potassium

🧠 Rationale: Furosemide is a loop diuretic that makes the kidneys flush out water and sodium.

Potassium is lost too.

Low potassium can cause muscle weakness and dangerous heart rhythms.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Furosemide (Lasix)

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Loop diuretic

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Heart failure

🔹 Edema

🔹 High blood pressure

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Low potassium

🔹 Dehydration and low BP

🔹 Ringing in the ears with fast IV push

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check potassium before giving

✅ Weigh daily, track I and O

✅ Give early in the day to avoid night urination

🚑 When to escalate:

🔹 K+ under 3.5 mEq/L

🔹 Muscle cramps, weakness or irregular pulse

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

LOOP diuretics make you LOSE potassium!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Furosemide #Pharmacology #HeartFailure #Potassium #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: The nurse is teaching about heart attack warning signs. Which symptoms are more common in women than in men?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #323!

❤️ Not every heart attack looks like the movies!

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Fatigue, nausea, and jaw or back pain

🧠 Rationale: Women are more likely to have subtle heart attack symptoms.

These include fatigue, nausea, shortness of breath and jaw, neck or back pain.

These signs are often missed, which delays treatment.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: MI in Women

⚠️ Common Signs in Women:

🔹 Unusual fatigue

🔹 Nausea or indigestion

🔹 Shortness of breath

🔹 Jaw, neck or back pain

❤️ Classic Signs:

🔹 Chest pressure or tightness

🔹 Pain spreading to the left arm

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Get a 12-lead ECG fast

✅ Check troponin

✅ Never ignore vague symptoms

🚑 Emergency:

🔹 Call 911 for any possible MI symptoms

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Women whisper, men shout: listen for the quiet signs!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Cardiac #MyocardialInfarction #WomensHealth #HeartHealth #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: The nurse reviews an adult client's arterial blood gas. Which PaCO2 value is within the normal range?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #324!

🫁 ABGs scare everyone. Can you spot the normal one?

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — 40 mmHg

🧠 Rationale: Normal PaCO2 is 35 to 45 mmHg.

40 mmHg is right in the middle of the normal range.

PaCO2 is the respiratory part of the ABG.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: ABG Normal Values

🧪 Normal Ranges:

🔹 pH: 7.35 to 7.45

🔹 PaCO2: 35 to 45 mmHg

🔹 HCO3: 22 to 26 mEq/L

🔹 PaO2: 80 to 100 mmHg

⚠️ PaCO2 Changes:

🔹 Above 45: respiratory acidosis (hypoventilation)

🔹 Below 35: respiratory alkalosis (hyperventilation)

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check pH first

✅ Then match PaCO2 or HCO3 to the pH

✅ Treat the client, not just the numbers

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

CO2 is an ACID: more CO2 means more acid!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #ABG #Respiratory #AcidBase #CriticalCare #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: The nurse is reviewing insulin types. Which insulin is rapid-acting?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #325!

💉 Four insulins, only one works fast. Which one?

This is a HIGH-YIELD endocrine question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Insulin lispro

🧠 Rationale: Insulin lispro is rapid-acting.

It starts working in about 15 minutes, so it is given with meals.

Glargine and detemir are long-acting. NPH is intermediate-acting.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Insulin Types

⚡ Rapid-Acting:

🔹 Lispro, aspart, glulisine

🔹 Onset about 15 minutes

🔹 Give with meals

⏱️ Short-Acting:

🔹 Regular insulin

🔹 Onset 30 to 60 minutes

🔹 Can be given IV

🌤️ Intermediate-Acting:

🔹 NPH, cloudy

🔹 Peaks in 4 to 12 hours

🌙 Long-Acting:

🔹 Glargine, detemir

🔹 No real peak

🔹 Never mix with other insulins

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Food must be ready before rapid-acting insulin

✅ Watch for hypoglycemia at the peak

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

LISPRO = LIGHTNING fast!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Insulin #Diabetes #Endocrine #Pharmacology #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: The nurse is assessing a healthy newborn at rest. Which heart rate range is normal?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #326!

👶 Newborn hearts beat FAST, but how fast is normal?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — 110 to 160/min

🧠 Rationale: A normal newborn heart rate is about 110 to 160/min.

It may drop to about 100 while asleep and rise with crying.

Count the apical pulse for a full minute.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Newborn Vital Signs

❤️ Heart Rate:

🔹 110 to 160/min

🔹 Apical pulse for 1 full minute

🫁 Respirations:

🔹 30 to 60/min

🔹 Short pauses under 20 seconds can be normal

🌡️ Temperature:

🔹 Axillary 97.7 to 99.5°F

🔹 Keep baby warm: skin to skin

🚑 When to escalate:

🔹 Heart rate under 100 while awake

🔹 Grunting, flaring or retractions

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Newborns run 110 to 160: think a fast little engine!

photos.question: A client at 34 weeks of pregnancy comes for a checkup. Which finding suggests preeclampsia?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #327!

🤰 Some pregnancy changes are normal. One of these is NOT!

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — BP 152/98 mmHg with protein in urine

🧠 Rationale: Preeclampsia is new BP of 140/90 or higher after 20 weeks.

It often comes with protein in the urine.

Mild ankle swelling, a slightly faster heart rate and frequent urination are normal in pregnancy.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Preeclampsia

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 BP 140/90 or higher after 20 weeks

🔹 Protein in urine

🔹 Headache or vision changes

🔹 Upper right belly pain

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check BP and urine protein

✅ Monitor reflexes

✅ Watch for seizures

💊 Treatment:

🔹 Magnesium sulfate prevents seizures

🔹 Calcium gluconate is the antidote

🚑 When to escalate:

🔹 Severe headache, blurred vision or BP 160/110 or higher

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

After 20 weeks, 140/90 plus protein = think PREECLAMPSIA!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: A client with schizophrenia is starting olanzapine. Which should the nurse monitor most closely?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #328!

🧠 This antipsychotic works well, but watch the scale!

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Weight and blood glucose

🧠 Rationale: Olanzapine is a second generation (atypical) antipsychotic.

It often causes weight gain, high blood sugar and high cholesterol.

This is called metabolic syndrome.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Olanzapine (Zyprexa)

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Second generation antipsychotic

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Schizophrenia

🔹 Bipolar disorder

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Weight gain

🔹 High blood sugar

🔹 High cholesterol

🔹 Drowsiness

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check weight and BMI often

✅ Monitor glucose and lipids

✅ Teach healthy diet and exercise

🚑 When to escalate:

🔹 High fever with rigid muscles: possible NMS

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

ZYPREXA = Zzz and eXtra weight!
